description: EgoLife is a 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset collected over one week with six participants living together. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses recording approximately 8 hours of egocentric video daily, supplemented by 15 GoPro cameras and 2 mmWave devices for third-person perspectives. The dataset includes intensive annotations such as audio transcripts, visual-audio narrations, and the EgoLifeQA benchmark with 3,000 long-context question-answering tasks.
name: EgoLife Dataset
rai:annotationsPerItem: 500 QA pairs per participant (6 participants = 3,000 total QAs); 361K narration phrases; 25K merged captions; visual-audio captions derived from merged captions paired with frames at 1 FPS.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: QA annotations were filtered from ~100K AI-generated candidates to 500 per participant (less than 1% retained) through rigorous selection. Annotators also annotated whether audio was required to answer each question and specified the look-back time (certification length) necessary for retrieving the correct answer. Statistics are presented in Figure 6 showing distribution across question types and certification lengths.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom video editing software with dubbing functions (CapCut by ByteDance) for caption annotation; SRT files for QA annotation review.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotation: merged audio from six participants, applied speech recognition (Whisper) to generate timestamped transcripts, used open-source diarization algorithm to differentiate speakers, then human reviewers refined each track keeping only speech audible to each participant. Caption annotation: videos split into 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8x speed; annotators provided continuous narrations; narrations converted to text and reviewed for synchronization. QA annotation: GPT-4o generated ~100K timestamped questions per participant from visual-audio captions provided as SRT files; annotators filtered to questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior; refined to 500 QA per participant with multiple-choice distractors added by annotators.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is primarily in Chinese (single dominant language), limiting linguistic diversity. The dataset was collected in a single scenario (one house, one week), sacrificing some generalizability. The paper acknowledges: "we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario)." Plans exist to expand to broader languages, locations, and activities.
rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together for one week in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses capturing multimodal egocentric videos (~8 hours/day). 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data. Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes: egocentric video and audio from Meta Aria glasses (VRS format), third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras, IMU data, gaze data, millimeter-wave radar ADC data, and WiFi CSI data. Video+Audio stored as MP4, IMU and Gaze as CSV, Radar Signal Data as CSV, WiFi Signal Data as HDF5.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day period (one week); the main session spans more than 40 hours of activities collected over multiple consecutive days.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to a single language (primarily Chinese), a single scenario (one house), and six participants over one week. The paper notes plans to expand to broader languages, locations, and activities. EgoGPT struggles with speech understanding (human laughter and emotions), identity recognition over time, and the dataset's narrow setting limits generalizability.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos were split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed for annotation. For caption generation, representative frames were sampled at 1 FPS. Activity categorization was automatically performed using GPT-4o on visual-audio captions with timestamps. QA candidates were filtered from ~100K to 500 per participant (less than 1% retained).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing included: (1) EgoSync - synchronizing multi-source data (video, audio, IMU) from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras; (2) EgoBlur - privacy protection by blurring all participant faces, bystanders' faces, and vehicle license plates; (3) audio muting of sensitive segments; (4) screen privacy masking; (5) mmWave signal processing using CFAR detection algorithm; (6) WiFi CSI data extraction using AX-CSI platform.
rai:dataSocialImpact: EgoButler and EgoLifeQA could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life especially for individuals needing consistent support such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges. In educational and professional settings, egocentric AI could facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development. Privacy and ethical considerations must be addressed to ensure user autonomy and trust.
rai:dataUseCases: Egocentric life assistance (recalling past events, monitoring health habits, personalized recommendations), long-term behavior pattern understanding, interpersonal dynamics analysis, multimodal egocentric AI assistant development, long-context video question answering, human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, human-machine interaction research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o-mini (merging narration phrases into captions), GPT-4o (expanding merged captions into visual-audio captions; generating QA candidates; activity categorization), Whisper (speech recognition for transcript generation), open-source diarization algorithm (speaker differentiation).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains video recordings of participants' daily activities including personal conversations, locations, and behaviors. Faces of participants and bystanders were blurred, audio segments with sensitive content were muted, and screen content with private information was masked. All participants provided informed consent.

evidence.name: This effort resulted in the EgoLife Dataset, a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation.
evidence.description: This effort resulted in the EgoLife Dataset, a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation. Leveraging this dataset, we introduce EgoLifeQA, a suite of long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks designed to provide meaningful assistance in daily life.

evidence.isLiveDataset: The dataset consists of two data sessions with different temporal scales and annotation status. The main session has been fully annotated and synchronized and is described in detail in the main paper.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded the participants' activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis of daily events and interactions.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded the participants' activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis of daily events and interactions.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: File FormatsData files are stored in standard formats for easy accessibility: Video+Audio: MP4, IMU: CSV, Gaze: CSV, Radar Signal Data: CSV, WiFi Signal Data: HDF5, Annotations: JSON
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rigorous data cleaning process was implemented to ensure synchronization, participant privacy, and readiness for annotation and data release. The pipeline synchronizes multi-source data (video, audio, IMU) from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras using EgoSync codebase, processes them through privacy protection (EgoBlur), dense captioning (EgoCaption), and transcription (EgoTranscript) modules.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We started transcript annotation after synchronizing all the egocentric videos, merging audio tracks from six participants into one, and applying speech recognition to generate initial timestamped transcripts. Using an open-source diarization algorithm, we differentiated the speakers and produced a preliminary transcript with overlapping conversations. This 50-hour transcript was then reviewed for accuracy.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The captioning tool is a video editing software with dubbing functions. We split all the videos into 5-minute clips, which were slowed to 0.8× speed, allowing annotators to provide continuous, detailed narrations by talking without pauses for high information density.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Using GPT-4o-mini, we merged related phrases into 25K "merged captions," forming coherent sentences aligned with specific video segments. These captions were then expanded by pairing them with representative frames (sampled at 1 FPS) and corresponding transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o. The categorization is automatically performed using GPT-4o on visual-audio captions with timestamps.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: The EgoLife dataset is a collection of ultra-long, multi-participant video recordings captured from both first-person and third-person perspectives, enriched with synchronized multimodal signals. The dataset documents human daily activities in natural environments and supports research on human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, and human–machine interaction.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: The development of EgoButler and the EgoLifeQA dataset holds significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction, particularly in personalized assistance and context-aware applications. By enabling AI to understand long-term, egocentric perspectives, EgoButler could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life, especially for individuals needing consistent support, such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges.
evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Blurring of faces and identifiers: All participant faces were blurred to anonymize identities. Additionally, bystanders' faces and vehicle license plates appearing in the footage were thoroughly blurred. Audio muting: Sensitive audio segments containing private or potentially identifiable information were muted to ensure privacy.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: As the first step toward a realistic egocentric life assistant, we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario). However, we see great value in expanding the project while encouraging community contributions.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Looking ahead, we plan to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities, and develop more sophisticated models that push the boundaries of AI's ability to understand and enhance everyday life.
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: After a rigorous selection and refinement process, we filtered the 100K QA candidates down to 1K high-quality questions per participant—less than 1% of the original pool—for further meticulous revision. This final round of curation resulted in a carefully crafted set of 500 QA per participant.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The captioning tool is a video editing software with dubbing functions. We split all the videos into 5-minute clips, which were slowed to 0.8× speed, allowing annotators to provide continuous, detailed narrations by talking without pauses for high information density.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After a rigorous selection and refinement process, we filtered the 100K QA candidates down to 1K high-quality questions per participant—less than 1% of the original pool—for further meticulous revision. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions, formally establishing EgoLifeQA as a benchmark for multiple-choice question answering. Additionally, they annotated whether audio was required to answer the question and specified the look-back time (certification length) necessary for retrieving the correct answer.
evidence.license: By releasing our datasets, models, and benchmarks, we aim to stimulate further research in egocentric AI assistants.
